journal:
Everything we'd been training for all summer and it was down to the wire. There were a couple of players on their team who were very good at jabbing so I was trying my hardest to dribble it carefully, back and forth, switching across the body as deftly as I could. To onlookers it probably looked less than impressive but to me, it felt like a wild game of cat and mouse.

At last, after clearing their right back, I made a dart for the circle. Their sweeper came racing forward; coach had told us before about how he'd been scouted for the state team this year. I remember thinking he'd be a shoe-in for player of the game after tonights performance; but I was able to get just enough of a drag flick to clear the bulk of his stick. The familiar crack of the ball ricocheting off at an angle and straight past the keeper into the net, sending the whole crowd into a deafening roar of celebration.

That night I felt invincible, like the only thing that ever mattered and ever will, was scoring that goal.
